s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation
salient_findings: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on the arms and legs
Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on the right arm 2 months after initiation of immunotherapy
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
Patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Trial of oral terbinafine yielded no improvement
Biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation
Numerous eosinophils were present on biopsy
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Numerous eosinophils on biopsy and pruritic rash

shortlist.label: Pembrolizumab-induced rash
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and rash started after immunotherapy initiation

shortlist.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving ipilimumab and rash started after immunotherapy initiation

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous annular plaques on skin and perivascular inflammation on biopsy

shortlist.label: Fixed drug eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Rash started after initiation of new immunotherapy regimen and did not improve with oral terbinafine

raw.rationale: The patient's rash started 2 months after initiation of pembrolizumab and ipilimumab, suggesting a temporal relationship with the immunotherapy regimen. The presence of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy is consistent with an immune-mediated reaction, which is a known side effect of pembrolizumab.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
rejected.why: While the biopsy shows numerous eosinophils, the clinical presentation and temporal relationship with immunotherapy initiation more strongly support a drug-induced rash.

rejected.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
rejected.why: Although ipilimumab can also cause immune-mediated reactions, pembrolizumab is more commonly associated with skin toxicity, including rash.

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: The biopsy findings and clinical presentation do not specifically support this diagnosis, which is characterized by a distinctive annular pattern and often associated with underlying infections or inflammatory conditions.

rejected.label: Fixed drug eruption
rejected.why: The rash did not improve with withdrawal of terbinafine, and the temporal relationship with immunotherapy initiation suggests a reaction to pembrolizumab or ipilimumab rather than terbinafine.
